rationale:
Split into 5 children. The supplied proof of weighted_mono_cutoff_limit is five independent analytic obligations plus a short assembly. The children are:
(a) cutoff_seq (Steps 1–2): construct admissible C¹ cutoffs whose widths tend to 0.
(b) cutoff_integral (Steps 3–5): the radial-cutoff dominated-convergence lemma ∫φ_m(r/t)f dμ → ∫_{B_t}f dμ. Inside this node it is used three times: u at t = ρ, u at t = σ, and G at every τ.
(c) kernel_limit (Step 6): one-dimensional kernel analysis giving measurability, |k_m| ≤ 2ⁿσ^{-n}, the support property, and the pointwise limit 1_{(σ,ρ]}(s)s^{-n}. It takes the two-sided bounds of the parent's dependency weighted_mono_kernel_bounds as a hypothesis, so it does not depend on another DAG branch.
(d) kernel_term (Steps 7, 11): conclusion (ii) plus dominated convergence of ∫u q k_m(r) dμ, stated for an abstract kernel family.
(e) curvature_term (Steps 8, 10): conclusion (i) plus dominated convergence on (σ,ρ]. It uses cutoff_integral.
All children are independent except curvature_term → cutoff_integral, so the dependencies are acyclic.

Remaining proof of the selected node, which is the parent's Step 9:
1. ρ > 0. Put a := min(1, (R−ρ)/ρ) > 0. Then cutoff_seq gives φ_m, ε_m with ε_m → 0 and 0 < ε_m < a, so ε_m ≤ 1 and (1+ε_m)ρ < R. Each φ_m is C¹ and antitone, equals 1 on t ≤ 1 and 0 on t ≥ 1+ε_m, and 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1. Hence (S_{φ_m}) holds for every m.
2. u is μ-integrable on B_R(ξ) by IntegrableOn.of_bound: |u| ≤ A, u is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B_R, and μ(B_R) < ∞.
3. weighted_mono_kernel_bounds gives the kernel squeeze for each m and s > 0. kernel_limit then gives its four conclusions; the vanishing for s > (1+ε_m)ρ implies vanishing for s > R.
4. kernel_term with C := 2ⁿ/σⁿ gives (ii) and the limit of the kernel term.
5. curvature_term (Continuous from C¹, (1+ε_m)ρ ≤ R) gives (i) and the limit of the curvature term.
6. cutoff_integral with f = u at t = ρ and t = σ gives the limit of the left side. This uses (1+ε_m)σ ≤ (1+ε_m)ρ < R, Measurable from C¹, and u·φ = φ·u.
7. Both sides of (S_{φ_m}) agree for every m, so tendsto_nhds_unique gives (iii).

subproblems.title: Admissible C¹ cutoff sequence with widths tending to zero (parent Steps 1–2)
subproblems.statement: For every real a > 0 there exist functions φ_m: ℝ → ℝ and reals ε_m (m ∈ ℕ) such that ε_m → 0 as m → ∞ and, for every m: 0 < ε_m < a; φ_m is of class C¹; φ_m is nonincreasing; φ_m(t) = 1 for all t ≤ 1; φ_m(t) = 0 for all t ≥ 1 + ε_m; and 0 ≤ φ_m(t) ≤ 1 for all t ∈ ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (a : ℝ), 0 < a → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ m, 0 < ε m ∧ ε m < a ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ m) ∧ Antitone (φ m) ∧ (∀ t, t ≤ 1 → φ m t = 1) ∧ (∀ t, 1 + ε m ≤ t → φ m t = 0) ∧ (∀ t, 0 ≤ φ m t ∧ φ m t ≤ 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ψ := Real.smoothTransition. (Context only: this is the cutoff φ_ε(t) = 1 − ψ((t − 1)/ε) of Steps 1–2 of the parent proof, with the explicit widths ε_m := a/(m + 2); nothing beyond the facts listed below is used.)
1. (Facts about ψ.) ψ: ℝ → ℝ is C^∞ (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff), monotone (Real.smoothTransition.monotone), ψ(x) = 0 for x ≤ 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos), ψ(x) = 1 for x ≥ 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le), and 0 ≤ ψ(x) ≤ 1 for every x (Real.smoothTransition.nonneg, Real.smoothTransition.le_one).
2. (Definitions.) For m ∈ ℕ put ε_m := a/(m + 2) and φ_m(t) := 1 − ψ((t − 1)/ε_m).
3. (Widths.) Since m + 2 ≥ 2 > 0 and a > 0, ε_m > 0. Multiplying by m + 2 > 0, ε_m < a ⟺ a < a(m + 2), which holds because a(m + 2) − a = a(m + 1) > 0. Finally m + 2 → +∞ as m → ∞ (the natural numbers tend to +∞ in ℝ and adding the constant 2 preserves this), so ε_m = a/(m + 2) → 0 (a constant divided by a sequence tending to +∞ tends to 0; Filter.Tendsto.const_div_atTop).
4. (C¹.) t ↦ (t − 1)/ε_m is affine, hence C^∞; ψ is C^∞, so the composition t ↦ ψ((t − 1)/ε_m) is C^∞, and so is t ↦ 1 − ψ((t − 1)/ε_m) (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.sub, ContDiff.div_const). In particular φ_m is C¹.
5. (Nonincreasing.) If s ≤ t then s − 1 ≤ t − 1 and, ε_m being positive, (s − 1)/ε_m ≤ (t − 1)/ε_m; by monotonicity of ψ, ψ((s − 1)/ε_m) ≤ ψ((t − 1)/ε_m), i.e. φ_m(t) ≤ φ_m(s).
6. (Plateau.) If t ≤ 1 then t − 1 ≤ 0 and ε_m > 0, so (t − 1)/ε_m ≤ 0, hence ψ((t − 1)/ε_m) = 0 and φ_m(t) = 1 − 0 = 1.
7. (Vanishing.) If t ≥ 1 + ε_m then t − 1 ≥ ε_m > 0, so (t − 1)/ε_m ≥ 1, hence ψ((t − 1)/ε_m) = 1 and φ_m(t) = 1 − 1 = 0.
8. (Range.) From 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1 we get 0 ≤ 1 − ψ((t − 1)/ε_m) ≤ 1, i.e. 0 ≤ φ_m(t) ≤ 1 for every t.
9. (Conclusion.) The families φ := (m ↦ φ_m) and ε := (m ↦ ε_m) satisfy ε_m → 0 by 3 and, for every m, all the listed properties by 3–8.
proof_key_steps: ψ = Real.smoothTransition is C^∞, monotone, 0 on (−∞,0], 1 on [1,∞), with values in [0,1]
Define ε_m = a/(m+2) and φ_m(t) = 1 − ψ((t−1)/ε_m)
0 < ε_m < a and ε_m → 0 (constant over a sequence tending to +∞)
φ_m is C¹ and nonincreasing (composition with an increasing affine map)
φ_m = 1 on t ≤ 1, φ_m = 0 on t ≥ 1+ε_m, and 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence for radial cutoff integrals (parent Steps 3–5)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), μ a measure on E, f: E → ℝ μ-integrable on the closed ball B_R(ξ), ξ ∈ E, and t, R ∈ ℝ with t > 0. Let φ_m: ℝ → ℝ (m ∈ ℕ) be Borel measurable and ε_m ∈ ℝ with ε_m → 0, (1 + ε_m)t ≤ R for every m, 0 ≤ φ_m(s) ≤ 1 for all s, φ_m(s) = 1 for s ≤ 1 and φ_m(s) = 0 for s ≥ 1 + ε_m. Then ∫ φ_m(|x − ξ|/t)·f(x) dμ(x) → ∫_{B_t(ξ)} f dμ as m → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (f : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (t R : ℝ) (φ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ), 0 < t → IntegrableOn f (closedBall ξ R) μ → Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ m, (1 + ε m) * t ≤ R) → (∀ m, Measurable (φ m)) → (∀ m s, 0 ≤ φ m s ∧ φ m s ≤ 1) → (∀ m s, s ≤ 1 → φ m s = 1) → (∀ m s, 1 + ε m ≤ s → φ m s = 0) → Tendsto (fun m ↦ ∫ x, φ m (‖x - ξ‖ / t) * f x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in closedBall ξ t, f x ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball, so x ∈ B_s(ξ) ⟺ |x − ξ| ≤ s (dist x ξ = |x − ξ|); r = r(x) := |x − ξ| ≥ 0; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; 1_S is the indicator function of S. Put B := B_R(ξ) and F_m(x) := φ_m(r(x)/t)·f(x). (Context only: Steps 3–5 of the parent proof, for a general integrable f and a general radius t; no positivity of ε_m is needed.)
1. (Vanishing off B.) Let x ∉ B, i.e. r(x) > R. For every m, (1 + ε_m)t ≤ R < r(x); dividing by t > 0 gives r(x)/t > 1 + ε_m, in particular r(x)/t ≥ 1 + ε_m, so φ_m(r(x)/t) = 0 and F_m(x) = 0.
2. (Measurability.) By 1, F_m = 1_B·F_m. The map x ↦ φ_m(r(x)/t) is Borel measurable (φ_m is measurable and x ↦ |x − ξ|/t is continuous), and f is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B because f is μ-integrable on B; hence the product F_m is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B. Since B is a closed, hence measurable, set, 1_B·F_m is a.e. strongly measurable for μ (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff); that is, F_m is a.e. strongly measurable for μ, for every m.
3. (Domination.) Put g := 1_B·|f|. For x ∈ B, |F_m(x)| = φ_m(r(x)/t)·|f(x)| ≤ |f(x)| = g(x) because 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1; for x ∉ B, |F_m(x)| = 0 = g(x) by 1. So |F_m| ≤ g on E for every m. Since |f| is μ-integrable on B, g is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff).
4. (Pointwise limit.) Fix x ∈ E. If x ∈ B_t(ξ) then r(x) ≤ t, so r(x)/t ≤ 1 (t > 0) and φ_m(r(x)/t) = 1 for every m; thus F_m(x) = f(x) for every m and F_m(x) → f(x) = 1_{B_t(ξ)}(x)f(x). If x ∉ B_t(ξ) then r(x) > t, so δ := r(x)/t − 1 > 0; since ε_m → 0 there is m₀ with ε_m < δ for all m ≥ m₀, i.e. r(x)/t > 1 + ε_m, hence φ_m(r(x)/t) = 0 and F_m(x) = 0 for m ≥ m₀; thus F_m(x) → 0 = 1_{B_t(ξ)}(x)f(x). Hence F_m → 1_{B_t(ξ)}·f pointwise on E.
5. (Dominated convergence.) By 2, 3 and 4, the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence with bound g and the filter atTop on ℕ) gives ∫F_m dμ → ∫1_{B_t(ξ)}·f dμ. Since B_t(ξ) is measurable, ∫1_{B_t(ξ)}·f dμ = ∫_{B_t(ξ)} f dμ (integral_indicator). This is the claim.
proof_key_steps: φ_m(r/t) = 0 off B_R(ξ) because (1+ε_m)t ≤ R and t > 0
F_m = 1_{B_R} F_m is μ-a.e. strongly measurable
|F_m| ≤ 1_{B_R}|f|, which is μ-integrable
F_m → 1_{B_t(ξ)} f pointwise, using ε_m → 0 off B_t(ξ)
Dominated convergence and ∫1_{B_t}f dμ = ∫_{B_t}f dμ

subproblems.title: Uniform bound, support and pointwise limit of the monotonicity kernels (parent Step 6)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, σ, ρ ∈ ℝ with 0 < σ ≤ ρ, and for m ∈ ℕ let φ_m: ℝ → ℝ be nonincreasing and ε_m ∈ ℝ with ε_m → 0, 0 < ε_m ≤ 1, φ_m(t) = 1 for t ≤ 1 and φ_m(t) = 0 for t ≥ 1 + ε_m. Put k_m(s) := ∫_{(σ,ρ]} −(s/τ²)·φ_m'(s/τ)/τⁿ dτ, where φ_m' := deriv φ_m, and D_m(s) := φ_m(s/ρ) − φ_m(s/σ). Assume that for all m and all s > 0, D_m(s)/sⁿ ≤ k_m(s) ≤ (1 + ε_m)ⁿ·(D_m(s)/sⁿ). Then: (1) every k_m is Borel measurable; (2) |k_m(s)| ≤ 2ⁿ/σⁿ for all m and all s ≥ 0; (3) k_m(s) = 0 for all m and all s > (1 + ε_m)ρ; (4) for every s ≥ 0, k_m(s) → 1_{(σ,ρ]}(s)·(sⁿ)^{-1} as m → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (σ ρ : ℝ) (φ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ), 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ m, 0 < ε m ∧ ε m ≤ 1) → (∀ m, Antitone (φ m)) → (∀ m t, t ≤ 1 → φ m t = 1) → (∀ m t, 1 + ε m ≤ t → φ m t = 0) → (∀ m s, 0 < s → (φ m (s / ρ) - φ m (s / σ)) / s ^ n ≤ ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, -(s / τ ^ 2) * deriv (φ m) (s / τ) / τ ^ n ∧ ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, -(s / τ ^ 2) * deriv (φ m) (s / τ) / τ ^ n ≤ (1 + ε m) ^ n * ((φ m (s / ρ) - φ m (s / σ)) / s ^ n)) → (∀ m, Measurable (fun s ↦ ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, -(s / τ ^ 2) * deriv (φ m) (s / τ) / τ ^ n)) ∧ (∀ m s, 0 ≤ s → |∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, -(s / τ ^ 2) * deriv (φ m) (s / τ) / τ ^ n| ≤ 2 ^ n / σ ^ n) ∧ (∀ m s, (1 + ε m) * ρ < s → ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, -(s / τ ^ 2) * deriv (φ m) (s / τ) / τ ^ n = 0) ∧ (∀ s, 0 ≤ s → Tendsto (fun m ↦ ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, -(s / τ ^ 2) * deriv (φ m) (s / τ) / τ ^ n) atTop (𝓝 ((Ioc σ ρ).indicator (fun s ↦ (s ^ n)⁻¹) s)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(σ,ρ]} is the integral against λ⌞(σ,ρ] (Ioc σ ρ); φ_m' := deriv φ_m; K_m(s, τ) := −(s/τ²)·φ_m'(s/τ)/τⁿ, so k_m(s) = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} K_m(s, τ)dτ; D_m(s) := φ_m(s/ρ) − φ_m(s/σ); κ(s) := 1_{(σ,ρ]}(s)·(sⁿ)^{-1}. The two-sided bound is a HYPOTHESIS of this lemma (in the parent it is supplied by weighted_mono_kernel_bounds, a dependency of the parent node that is not available here and needs C¹, which is not assumed); use the hypothesis directly. (Context: Step 6 of the parent proof.) Note ρ ≥ σ > 0.
0. (Range of φ_m.) For every t: φ_m(t) ≤ φ_m(min(t, 1)) = 1, because min(t, 1) ≤ t, φ_m is nonincreasing and min(t, 1) ≤ 1; and φ_m(t) ≥ φ_m(max(t, 1 + ε_m)) = 0, because max(t, 1 + ε_m) ≥ t and max(t, 1 + ε_m) ≥ 1 + ε_m. So 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1.
1. (Properties of D_m.) Let s > 0. (a) Since 0 < σ ≤ ρ, s/ρ ≤ s/σ, so φ_m(s/ρ) ≥ φ_m(s/σ) and D_m(s) ≥ 0; by 0, D_m(s) ≤ 1 − 0 = 1. (b) If s ≤ σ, then s/σ ≤ 1 and s/ρ ≤ 1 (as s ≤ σ ≤ ρ), so D_m(s) = 1 − 1 = 0. (c) If s > (1 + ε_m)ρ, then (dividing by ρ > 0) s/ρ ≥ 1 + ε_m and, by (a), s/σ ≥ s/ρ ≥ 1 + ε_m, so D_m(s) = 0 − 0 = 0.
2. (Squeeze to zero.) If s > 0 and D_m(s) = 0, the assumed bounds read 0 = 0/sⁿ ≤ k_m(s) ≤ (1 + ε_m)ⁿ·0 = 0, so k_m(s) = 0.
3. (k_m(0) = 0.) For s = 0 the integrand is −(0/τ²)·φ_m'(0/τ)/τⁿ = 0 for every τ, so k_m(0) = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} 0 dτ = 0.
4. (Claim (1): measurability.) For any function φ_m: ℝ → ℝ, deriv φ_m is Borel measurable (measurable_deriv). The map (s, τ) ↦ K_m(s, τ) on ℝ × ℝ is obtained from the coordinate projections, the quotient s/τ, deriv φ_m, powers, products, negation and quotients, all of which are Borel measurable on ℝ (division on ℝ is measurable, with x/0 = 0); hence K_m is Borel measurable, so strongly measurable, on ℝ × ℝ. The measure λ⌞(σ,ρ] is s-finite (indeed finite), so s ↦ ∫K_m(s, τ) d(λ⌞(σ,ρ])(τ) = k_m(s) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right), hence measurable.
5. (Claim (2): uniform bound.) Let s ≥ 0. If s = 0, |k_m(0)| = 0 ≤ 2ⁿ/σⁿ by 3. If 0 < s ≤ σ, k_m(s) = 0 by 1(b) and 2, so |k_m(s)| = 0 ≤ 2ⁿ/σⁿ. If s > σ: by 1(a) and the lower bound, k_m(s) ≥ D_m(s)/sⁿ ≥ 0, so |k_m(s)| = k_m(s) ≤ (1 + ε_m)ⁿ·(D_m(s)/sⁿ). Now 0 ≤ 1 + ε_m ≤ 2 (as 0 < ε_m ≤ 1), so (1 + ε_m)ⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ; and D_m(s)/sⁿ ≤ 1/sⁿ ≤ 1/σⁿ because 0 ≤ D_m(s) ≤ 1 and sⁿ ≥ σⁿ > 0. Multiplying these inequalities between nonnegative quantities gives k_m(s) ≤ 2ⁿ·(1/σⁿ) = 2ⁿ/σⁿ.
6. (Claim (3): support.) If s > (1 + ε_m)ρ, then s > 0 (since (1 + ε_m)ρ > 0) and D_m(s) = 0 by 1(c), so k_m(s) = 0 by 2.
7. (Claim (4): pointwise limit.) Fix s ≥ 0. (a) s = 0: k_m(0) = 0 for every m by 3, and 0 ∉ (σ, ρ] because σ > 0, so κ(0) = 0; the constant sequence 0 converges to κ(0). (b) 0 < s ≤ σ: k_m(s) = 0 for every m by 1(b) and 2, and s ∉ (σ, ρ], so κ(s) = 0. (c) σ < s ≤ ρ: here κ(s) = (sⁿ)^{-1}. Since s/σ > 1 and ε_m → 0, there is m₀ with ε_m < s/σ − 1 for m ≥ m₀; for such m, φ_m(s/σ) = 0 while φ_m(s/ρ) = 1 (as s/ρ ≤ 1), so D_m(s) = 1 and the assumed bounds give (sⁿ)^{-1} ≤ k_m(s) ≤ (1 + ε_m)ⁿ·(1/sⁿ). As m → ∞, 1 + ε_m → 1, so (1 + ε_m)ⁿ → 1ⁿ = 1 (continuity of t ↦ tⁿ) and the upper bound tends to 1/sⁿ = (sⁿ)^{-1}; the lower bound is constant. By the squeeze theorem with eventual inequalities (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'), k_m(s) → (sⁿ)^{-1} = κ(s). (d) s > ρ: κ(s) = 0. Since s/ρ > 1 and s/σ > 1 (because s > ρ ≥ σ), there is m₀ with ε_m < s/ρ − 1 and ε_m < s/σ − 1 for m ≥ m₀; for such m, φ_m(s/ρ) = φ_m(s/σ) = 0, so D_m(s) = 0 and k_m(s) = 0 by 2. Hence k_m(s) is eventually 0 and tends to 0 = κ(s). In all cases k_m(s) → κ(s) = (Ioc σ ρ).indicator (s ↦ (sⁿ)^{-1}) (s).
proof_key_steps: 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1 from antitonicity and the boundary values; 0 ≤ D_m(s) ≤ 1 for s > 0
D_m(s) = 0 for 0 < s ≤ σ and for s > (1+ε_m)ρ, and then the assumed kernel squeeze forces k_m(s) = 0; k_m(0) = 0
k_m is measurable: the integrand is Borel on ℝ² (measurable_deriv) and StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right
|k_m(s)| ≤ (1+ε_m)ⁿ s^{-n} ≤ 2ⁿσ^{-n} for s > σ, and k_m(s) = 0 otherwise
Pointwise limit by cases s = 0, 0 < s ≤ σ, σ < s ≤ ρ (squeeze with (1+ε_m)ⁿ → 1), s > ρ, using ε_m → 0

subproblems.title: Annulus term: integrability and dominated convergence of the kernel integrals (parent Steps 7 and 11)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), μ a measure on E that is finite on compact sets, u, q: E → ℝ, ξ ∈ E and σ, ρ, R, A, C ∈ ℝ with σ > 0 and ρ ≤ R; u and q a.e. strongly measurable for μ restricted to B_R(ξ); |u(x)| ≤ A and |q(x)| ≤ 1 for x ∈ B_R(ξ). Let k_m: ℝ → ℝ (m ∈ ℕ) be Borel measurable with |k_m(s)| ≤ C for all s ≥ 0, k_m(s) = 0 for all s > R, and k_m(s) → 1_{(σ,ρ]}(s)·(sⁿ)^{-1} as m → ∞ for every s ≥ 0. Then x ↦ u(x)·(q(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ) is μ-integrable on B_ρ(ξ) ∖ B_σ(ξ), and ∫ u(x)·q(x)·k_m(|x − ξ|) dμ(x) → ∫_{B_ρ(ξ)∖B_σ(ξ)} u(x)·(q(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ) dμ(x) as m → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (u q : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (σ ρ R A C : ℝ) (k : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → 0 < σ → ρ ≤ R → AEStronglyMeasurable u (μ.restrict (closedBall ξ R)) → AEStronglyMeasurable q (μ.restrict (closedBall ξ R)) → (∀ x ∈ closedBall ξ R, |u x| ≤ A ∧ |q x| ≤ 1) → (∀ m, Measurable (k m)) → (∀ m s, 0 ≤ s → |k m s| ≤ C) → (∀ m s, R < s → k m s = 0) → (∀ s, 0 ≤ s → Tendsto (fun m ↦ k m s) atTop (𝓝 ((Ioc σ ρ).indicator (fun s ↦ (s ^ n)⁻¹) s))) → IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ u x * (q x / ‖x - ξ‖ ^ n)) (closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ) μ ∧ Tendsto (fun m ↦ ∫ x, u x * q x * k m ‖x - ξ‖ ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ, u x * (q x / ‖x - ξ‖ ^ n) ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball, so x ∈ B_s(ξ) ⟺ |x − ξ| ≤ s (dist x ξ = |x − ξ|); r = r(x) := |x − ξ| ≥ 0; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; 1_S is the indicator function of S. Put B := B_R(ξ), Ann := B_ρ(ξ) ∖ B_σ(ξ), κ(s) := 1_{(σ,ρ]}(s)·(sⁿ)^{-1} and F_m(x) := u(x)·q(x)·k_m(r(x)). (Context: Steps 7 and 11 of the parent proof, with the kernel properties of its Step 6 taken as hypotheses.)
0. (Preliminaries.) E is finite-dimensional, so closed balls are compact and μ(B) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top, μ finite on compacts). For x ∈ E: x ∈ Ann ⟺ (r(x) ≤ ρ and not r(x) ≤ σ) ⟺ σ < r(x) ≤ ρ ⟺ r(x) ∈ (σ, ρ]. Since ρ ≤ R, Ann ⊆ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ B. Ann is measurable (difference of two closed sets).
1. (First conclusion: integrability on the annulus.) Let x ∈ Ann. Then x ∈ B, so |u(x)| ≤ A (in particular A ≥ 0) and |q(x)| ≤ 1; and r(x) > σ > 0, so r(x)ⁿ ≥ σⁿ > 0. Hence |u(x)·(q(x)/r(x)ⁿ)| = |u(x)|·(|q(x)|/r(x)ⁿ) ≤ A·(1/r(x)ⁿ) ≤ A·(1/σⁿ) = A/σⁿ. The function x ↦ u(x)·(q(x)/r(x)ⁿ) is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞Ann: u and q are a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B and μ⌞Ann ≤ μ⌞B (Ann ⊆ B), so they are a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞Ann; x ↦ r(x)ⁿ is continuous; and products and quotients of a.e. strongly measurable real functions are a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul, AEStronglyMeasurable.div₀). Since μ(Ann) ≤ μ(B) < ∞ and the bound A/σⁿ holds μ⌞Ann-a.e. (indeed at every point of Ann), the function is μ-integrable on Ann (IntegrableOn.of_bound).
2. (Vanishing off B.) If x ∉ B then r(x) > R, so k_m(r(x)) = 0 and F_m(x) = 0 for every m.
3. (Measurability.) By 2, F_m = 1_B·F_m. On B, F_m is the product of u and q, which are a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B, and of k_m∘r, which is Borel measurable (k_m measurable, r continuous); so F_m is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B, and since B is closed (measurable), 1_B·F_m = F_m is a.e. strongly measurable for μ (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff).
4. (Domination.) Let g := 1_B·(A·C), i.e. the constant A·C on B and 0 off B; g is μ-integrable because μ(B) < ∞. For x ∈ B: |u(x)|·|q(x)| ≤ |u(x)|·1 ≤ A, |k_m(r(x))| ≤ C (as r(x) ≥ 0), and A ≥ |u(x)| ≥ 0, so |F_m(x)| = (|u(x)|·|q(x)|)·|k_m(r(x))| ≤ A·C = g(x). For x ∉ B, |F_m(x)| = 0 = g(x) by 2.
5. (Pointwise limit.) Fix x. Since r(x) ≥ 0, k_m(r(x)) → κ(r(x)), so F_m(x) → u(x)·q(x)·κ(r(x)). If x ∈ Ann then r(x) ∈ (σ, ρ] and u(x)·q(x)·κ(r(x)) = u(x)·q(x)·(r(x)ⁿ)^{-1} = u(x)·(q(x)/r(x)ⁿ); if x ∉ Ann then r(x) ∉ (σ, ρ] and u(x)·q(x)·κ(r(x)) = 0. Hence F_m → 1_{Ann}·(x ↦ u(x)·(q(x)/r(x)ⁿ)) pointwise on E.
6. (Second conclusion.) By 3, 4 and 5, dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence with bound g) gives ∫F_m dμ → ∫1_{Ann}·u·(q/rⁿ) dμ, and ∫1_{Ann}·u·(q/rⁿ) dμ = ∫_{Ann} u·(q/rⁿ) dμ because Ann is measurable (integral_indicator).
proof_key_steps: μ(B_R(ξ)) < ∞, annulus ⊆ B_R(ξ), and x ∈ annulus ⟺ |x−ξ| ∈ (σ,ρ]
On the annulus |u·(q/rⁿ)| ≤ A/σⁿ, so the limit integrand is μ-integrable there
u·q·k_m(r) vanishes off B_R(ξ), is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and is dominated by A·C·1_{B_R(ξ)}
Pointwise limit u·q·κ(r) = 1_annulus·u·(q/rⁿ)
Dominated convergence plus integral_indicator

subproblems.title: Curvature term: integrability of τ^{-n-1}∫_{B_τ}G and convergence of the smoothed τ-integrals (parent Steps 8 and 10)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), μ a measure on E, G: E → ℝ μ-integrable on the closed ball B_R(ξ), ξ ∈ E, and σ, ρ, R ∈ ℝ with 0 < σ ≤ ρ. Let φ_m: ℝ → ℝ (m ∈ ℕ) be continuous and ε_m ∈ ℝ with ε_m → 0, ε_m > 0, (1 + ε_m)ρ ≤ R, 0 ≤ φ_m(s) ≤ 1 for all s, φ_m(s) = 1 for s ≤ 1 and φ_m(s) = 0 for s ≥ 1 + ε_m. Then τ ↦ (∫_{B_τ(ξ)} G dμ)/τⁿ⁺¹ is integrable on (σ, ρ], and ∫_{(σ,ρ]} (∫ φ_m(|x − ξ|/τ)·G(x) dμ(x))/τⁿ⁺¹ dτ → ∫_{(σ,ρ]} (∫_{B_τ(ξ)} G dμ)/τⁿ⁺¹ dτ as m → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (G : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (σ ρ R : ℝ) (φ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ), 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → IntegrableOn G (closedBall ξ R) μ → Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ m, 0 < ε m) → (∀ m, (1 + ε m) * ρ ≤ R) → (∀ m, Continuous (φ m)) → (∀ m s, 0 ≤ φ m s ∧ φ m s ≤ 1) → (∀ m s, s ≤ 1 → φ m s = 1) → (∀ m s, 1 + ε m ≤ s → φ m s = 0) → IntegrableOn (fun τ ↦ (∫ x in closedBall ξ τ, G x ∂μ) / τ ^ (n + 1)) (Ioc σ ρ) ∧ Tendsto (fun m ↦ ∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, (∫ x, φ m (‖x - ξ‖ / τ) * G x ∂μ) / τ ^ (n + 1)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ τ in Ioc σ ρ, (∫ x in closedBall ξ τ, G x ∂μ) / τ ^ (n + 1)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball, so x ∈ B_s(ξ) ⟺ |x − ξ| ≤ s (dist x ξ = |x − ξ|); r = r(x) := |x − ξ| ≥ 0; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; 1_S is the indicator function of S. Put B := B_R(ξ), L_m(τ) := ∫φ_m(r(x)/τ)·G(x) dμ(x), L(τ) := ∫_{B_τ(ξ)} G dμ, h_m(τ) := L_m(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹, h(τ) := L(τ)/τⁿ⁺¹ and ν := λ⌞(σ,ρ]. (Context: Steps 8 and 10 of the parent proof.) Note ρ ≥ σ > 0 and 1 + ε_m > 0.
1. (Vanishing off B.) Let 0 < τ ≤ ρ and x ∉ B, i.e. r(x) > R. Then (1 + ε_m)τ ≤ (1 + ε_m)ρ ≤ R < r(x), so dividing by τ > 0, r(x)/τ ≥ 1 + ε_m and φ_m(r(x)/τ) = 0.
2. (Measurability and domination in x.) Let g := 1_B·|G|, which is μ-integrable since G is μ-integrable on B. For 0 < τ ≤ ρ put F_τ(x) := φ_m(r(x)/τ)·G(x). By 1, F_τ = 1_B·F_τ; on B, F_τ is the product of the Borel function x ↦ φ_m(r(x)/τ) (φ_m continuous) and of G, which is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B; so F_τ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B, and hence (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff, B closed) F_τ = 1_B·F_τ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ. Moreover |F_τ(x)| ≤ g(x) for all x: on B because 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1, and off B because F_τ(x) = 0 by 1.
3. (Uniform bound for L_m.) Put C_G := ∫g dμ ≥ 0. For 0 < τ ≤ ρ, |L_m(τ)| ≤ C_G by 2 (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).
4. (Continuity of L_m.) L_m is continuous on [σ, ρ] by continuity of parameter integrals under domination (continuousOn_of_dominated with bound g): for τ ∈ [σ, ρ] we have 0 < τ ≤ ρ, so by 2 F_τ is a.e. strongly measurable and |F_τ| ≤ g with g integrable; and for every x the map τ ↦ φ_m(r(x)/τ)·G(x) is continuous on [σ, ρ] because τ ↦ r(x)/τ is continuous on [σ, ρ] (τ ≠ 0 there) and φ_m is continuous.
5. (Measurability of h_m.) τ ↦ τⁿ⁺¹ is continuous and nonzero on [σ, ρ], so h_m is continuous on [σ, ρ] ⊇ (σ, ρ], hence a.e. strongly measurable for ν (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable, (σ, ρ] measurable).
6. (Pointwise convergence.) Let τ ∈ (σ, ρ]. Then τ > 0 and (1 + ε_m)τ ≤ (1 + ε_m)ρ ≤ R for every m, and each φ_m is measurable (being continuous). The sibling lemma weighted_mono_cutoff_integral_tendsto, applied with f := G, t := τ and the same R, φ_m, ε_m (its hypotheses: τ > 0; G is μ-integrable on B_R(ξ); ε_m → 0; (1 + ε_m)τ ≤ R; φ_m measurable; 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1; φ_m(s) = 1 for s ≤ 1; φ_m(s) = 0 for s ≥ 1 + ε_m), gives L_m(τ) → L(τ). Dividing by the constant τⁿ⁺¹ ≠ 0, h_m(τ) → h(τ).
7. (Uniform bound for h_m.) For τ ∈ (σ, ρ]: |h_m(τ)| = |L_m(τ)|/τⁿ⁺¹ ≤ C_G/τⁿ⁺¹ ≤ C_G/σⁿ⁺¹, by 3, τⁿ⁺¹ ≥ σⁿ⁺¹ > 0 and C_G ≥ 0.
8. (First conclusion: integrability.) By 5 and 6, h is the ν-a.e. pointwise limit (indeed the limit at every point of (σ, ρ]) of the ν-a.e. strongly measurable functions h_m, so h is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae). For τ ∈ (σ, ρ], |h(τ)| = lim |h_m(τ)| ≤ C_G/σⁿ⁺¹ by 6 and 7 (le_of_tendsto). Since λ((σ, ρ]) = ρ − σ < ∞, h is integrable on (σ, ρ] (IntegrableOn.of_bound).
9. (Second conclusion: convergence.) The constant function C_G/σⁿ⁺¹ is ν-integrable because ν is finite. By 5 (measurability), 7 (domination ν-a.e.) and 6 (convergence ν-a.e.), dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) gives ∫_{(σ,ρ]} h_m dλ → ∫_{(σ,ρ]} h dλ, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: φ_m(r/τ) = 0 off B_R(ξ) for 0 < τ ≤ ρ; the x-integrand is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by 1_{B_R}|G|
|L_m(τ)| ≤ ∫_{B_R}|G| and L_m is continuous on [σ,ρ] (continuousOn_of_dominated), so h_m is a.e. strongly measurable
For τ ∈ (σ,ρ], L_m(τ) → ∫_{B_τ}G by the sibling cutoff_integral lemma
The limit τ^{-n-1}∫_{B_τ}G is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by C_G/σⁿ⁺¹, hence integrable on (σ,ρ]
Dominated convergence on (σ,ρ] with the constant bound C_G/σⁿ⁺¹
